questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Kuwait?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Kuwait article.

questions.proof: Arabic is mostly spoken in Kuwait but English is widespread among Kuwaitis (residents of Kuwait).

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “In 1990, _____ invaded (brought an army in to fight against) Kuwait.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “invaded”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Kuwait article.

questions.proof: In 1990, Iraq invaded (brought an army in to fight against) Kuwait.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “6 issued in _____, which divided Kuwait into three governorates: the Capital Governorate, Hawalli Governorate and Al-Ahmadi Governorate.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Governorates” part of the Kuwait article.

questions.proof: 6 issued in 1962, which divided Kuwait into three governorates: the Capital Governorate, Hawalli Governorate and Al-Ahmadi Governorate.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Per capita gross national income ($) in _____: 612.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twenty-first century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Kuwait article, under the heading “Demographics”.

questions.proof: Per capita gross national income ($) in 2002: 612.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Population density (per square kilometer) in _____: 107.4.”
